title: Are we becoming more allergic to food
titleChinese: 食物过敏越来越常见的原因
paragraphs: Do you love food? Whether you’re a foodie or someone who just likes eating, there is so much to choose from. We know that too much of the wrong kind of food can be bad for our health, but for some people having a food allergy means eating certain things can actually be harmful - and now, it seems, this is affecting more and more of us.

An allergy is caused by the immune system fighting substances in the environment, known as allergens, that it should see as harmless. Food allergies can cause life-threatening reactions, which means people have to spend their lives following strict dietary restrictions and worrying about the ingredients of everything they consume. Allergy specialist Dr Adam Fox says “if you look back over, say, 30 or 40 years… there are much more allergic problems around now than there were.”

We often hear about people having allergies to dairy products and to peanuts. Last year a 15-year-old girl died after suffering a fatal allergic reaction from eating a baguette containing sesame seeds. This led to a call for better food-labelling laws.

Research has found that this problem is particularly affecting children. More and more of them are having allergic reactions to certain foodstuffs. Writing for the BBC website, Dr Alexandra Santos from King's College London says “food allergy now affects about 7% of children in the UK and 9% of those in Australia, for example. Across Europe, 2% of adults have food allergies.”

So what might be the cause? Dr Santos says the increase in allergies is not simply the effect of society becoming more aware of them and better at diagnosing them; it seems to be more environmental. She says possible factors are “pollution, dietary changes and less exposure to microbes, which change how our immune systems respond.” She points out that it’s very common for migrants who move to another country to develop asthma and food allergies in their new location.
A lot of work is being done to try and find a cure, but that’s not easy. So for now allergy sufferers must watch what they eat and they must rely on clear and accurate labelling.

vocabulary.entry: food allergy /ˈfuːd ˈælədʒi/ 食物过敏
vocabulary.example: His food allergy means he can't eat anything with nuts in it.
vocabulary.translation: 他的食物过敏症让他不能吃任何含坚果的东西。

vocabulary.entry: immune system /ɪˈmjuːn ˈsɪstəm/ 免疫系统
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet is important for maintaining a healthy immune system.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡的饮食对维持免疫系统健康很重要。

vocabulary.example: Dust mites are one of the most common allergens in homes.
vocabulary.translation: 尘螨是家庭中最常见的过敏原之一。

vocabulary.entry: life-threatening /ˈlaɪf θretnɪŋ/ adj. 危及生命的
vocabulary.example: The patient is in a life-threatening condition and needs emergency surgery.
vocabulary.translation: 这名患者情况危急，需要进行紧急手术。

vocabulary.entry: dietary restriction /ˈdaɪətəri rɪˈstrɪkʃn/ 饮食限制

vocabulary.translation: 糖尿病患者需要遵守严格的饮食限制。

vocabulary.example: The main ingredient of this soup is chicken.
vocabulary.translation: 这道汤的主要原料是鸡肉。

vocabulary.translation: 我们每天都要喝很多水，尤其是在炎热的天气里。

vocabulary.translation: 奶酪、牛奶和酸奶都是常见的乳制品。

vocabulary.example: Peanut butter is a popular spread for bread in many countries.
vocabulary.translation: 花生酱在很多国家是很受欢迎的面包涂抹酱。

vocabulary.example: The driver suffered fatal injuries in the car accident.
vocabulary.translation: 这名司机在车祸中受了致命伤。

vocabulary.entry: baguette /bæˈɡet/ n. 法棍面包；长棍面包
vocabulary.example: She bought a fresh baguette from the bakery on her way home.
vocabulary.translation: 她在回家的路上从面包店买了一根新鲜的法棍面包。

vocabulary.example: Sesame seeds are often sprinkled on top of bread for extra flavor.
vocabulary.translation: 芝麻常被撒在面包表面来增加风味。

vocabulary.entry: food-labelling law /ˈfuːd ˈleɪblɪŋ lɔː/ 食品标签法规
vocabulary.example: The new food-labelling law requires all products to list their ingredients clearly.
vocabulary.translation: 新的食品标签法规要求所有产品都要清晰标注成分。

vocabulary.example: The shop sells a wide range of foodstuffs from different countries.
vocabulary.translation: 这家商店出售来自不同国家的各类食品。

vocabulary.example: The doctor was able to diagnose the disease quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 医生很快就诊断出了这种疾病。

vocabulary.example: Air pollution is a major problem in many big cities.
vocabulary.translation: 空气污染是很多大城市的主要问题。

vocabulary.example: Some microbes are beneficial to human health, while others are harmful.
vocabulary.translation: 有些微生物对人体健康有益，而有些则有害。

vocabulary.example: Many migrants come to this city to look for better job opportunities.
vocabulary.translation: 很多移民来到这座城市寻求更好的工作机会。

vocabulary.example: Cold air can trigger asthma attacks in some people.
vocabulary.translation: 冷空气可能会引发一些人的哮喘发作。

vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在努力寻找治疗癌症的方法。

vocabulary.entry: accurate /ˈækjərət/ adj. 准确的；精确的
vocabulary.example: You need to provide accurate information when filling out this form.
vocabulary.translation: 填写这份表格时，你需要提供准确的信息。
